lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Telluride Town Council's November 17 meeting, where the 2027 budget and property tax levy go to a vote alongside a second-reading ordinance that would suspend the Open Space Fund's 5% cut of Real Estate Transfer Tax revenue for the year — a real trade-off between tight finances and long-term land conservation. Meanwhile, San Miguel County's Planning Commission digs into proposed changes to the Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee on November 12, a wonky-sounding item with genuine consequences for how workforce housing gets built here. Rounding out the week, SMART's board acts on three resolutions including an amendment to the Executive Director's employment contract and an update on the gondola project.

notable.stake: Fee structure changes could shape whether workforce housing gets built countywide.
